title: Cacio e Pepe
subtitle: Roman pasta with cheese and black pepper
excerpt: Cacio e pepe is a Roman pasta dish that uses just three main ingredients: pasta, cheese, and black pepper. The magic is in the technique: a starchy pasta water emulsion binds the cheese into a silky, coating sauce with no cream needed.
sourceNotes: Cacio e pepe originates in Roman cucina povera. The name means cheese and pepper in Romanesco dialect. It has been a staple of Lazio cooking for centuries.

content.text: The sauce forms from starchy pasta water and finely grated cheese alone. Use a block of parmesan and grate it yourself on the finest side of a box grater. Pre-grated cheese will clump and not melt smoothly. Grind black pepper coarsely and toast it in the dry pan first to bring out its heat and aroma.
You will also need 2 teaspoons of coarsely ground black pepper and a generous amount of salt for the pasta water.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook the spaghetti until just under al dente, about 1 minute less than the pack says.
While the pasta cooks, toast the black pepper in the dry frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the butter and olive oil.
Scoop out 300ml of pasta water before draining. Keep it hot.
Drain the pasta. Add it to the frying pan off the heat. Pour in 100ml of pasta water.
Add three-quarters of the parmesan. Toss fast, adding more pasta water a splash at a time, until the sauce is glossy and coats every strand.
Divide between bowls. Add the rest of the parmesan and a little more black pepper to serve.

items.cause: Pan was too hot when you added the cheese.
items.fix: Take pan off heat fully before adding cheese.
Add more hot pasta water a splash at a time.
Toss over low heat for 30 seconds to tighten.
